                [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, crud } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask } from "./src/tasks" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create: { overrideFn: createTask },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'update: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'delete: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Real apps need things to happen on a timer — digest emails, cleanup, syncs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp models this with declarative **jobs** backed by a PgBoss executor.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You declare the job and its cron schedule in the spec:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, job } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { mySpecialJob } from "./src/workers/bar" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job(mySpecialJob, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: "PgBoss",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schedule: { cron: "0 * * * *", args: { name: "Johnny" } },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With the cron schedule in place, this runs automatically on the hour — no separate scheduler service to provision, no manual invocation.'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Wasp's Programmable Spec Lets You Build File-Based Routing in 45 Lines\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-24, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://www.devdigest.org/articles/wasps-programmable-spec-lets-you-build-file-based-routing-in-45-lines)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, it uses an explicit Spec file (`main.wasp.ts`) where you declare routes, auth, queries, and cron jobs in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'That Spec is now programmable—a standard Node.js program that can import npm packages, read the filesystem, or call APIs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The only requirement: export an `app` object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The simplest version:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { page, ref, route } from &#34;@wasp.sh/spec&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { pascalCase } from &#34;es-toolkit&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { globSync } from &#34;node:fs&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import * as path from &#34;node:path&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wiring it into your app is one line:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from &#34;@wasp.sh/spec&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { fileBasedRoutes } from &#34;./lib/file-based-routes.wasp&#34;;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'other config\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fileBasedRoutes(&#34;src&#34;),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// other spec items\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return route(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`${routeName}Route`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'page(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m');'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Function: app() | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/api/@wasp.sh/spec/functions/app)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a Wasp App.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### spec ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Spec`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The specification (Spec) of the app.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Build entries with the dedicated constructors (page, route, query, action, api, apiNamespace, job, crud).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Example ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { app, page, route } from '@wasp.sh/spec'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import MainPage from './src/MainPage' with { type: 'ref' }\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m"name: 'todoApp',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'wasp: { version: "^0.24.0" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'title: "ToDo App",\n'[39m +
                      [32m`head: ["<link rel='icon' href='/favicon.ico' />"],\n`[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m"route('MainRoute', '/', page(MainPage)),\n"[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Migrating from the Wasp TS Config\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|What|Before|After|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Imports|``` { import, from } ```|``` import { ... } from "./src/..." with { type: "ref" }; ```|\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Custom HTTP API Endpoints\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For these cases, you can use an\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'APIs are used to tie a JS function to a certain endpoint e.g.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'To create a Wasp API, you must:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'…\n'[39m +

                      [32m'First, we need to declare the API in the Wasp file and you can easily do this with the\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp Spec (main.wasp.ts)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-28, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/general/spec)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You define and configure the high level of your app (pages, routes, queries, actions, auth, ...) in a `main.wasp.ts` file in the root of your project.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call this file the **Wasp Spec**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You build your app by:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Importing the building blocks (`app`, `page`, `route`, `query`, ...) from `@wasp.sh/spec`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Importing your own components and functions adding the import attribute `with { type: "ref" }`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"3. Calling `app({ ... })` with your app's configuration, listing all the pages, routes, queries, actions, etc.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'in the `spec` property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Exporting the result as the **default export** of the file.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`spec` is short for specification: the pages, routes, queries, actions, APIs, jobs and CRUDs that make up your app.'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# File Uploads | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-13, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/guides/integrations/file-upload)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Install Multer​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Install the Multer package and its types:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install multer\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install --save-dev @types/multer\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define the API endpoint in main.wasp.ts​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Create an API namespace with middleware configuration and the upload endpoint:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api, apiNamespace, app, page, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { configureFileUploadMiddleware, uploadFile } from "./src/apis" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'route("RootRoute", "/", page(MainPage)),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'apiNamespace("/api/upload", { middlewareConfigFn: configureFileUploadMiddleware }),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'api("POST", "/api/upload", uploadFile),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- JavaScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- TypeScript'[39m

                content: [32m'const REGISTERED_METRICS = ["error_rate", "latency_ms", "queue_depth"];\n'[39m +

                  [32m'function roundHalfAway(val: number, decimals: number = 3): number {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'      const count = currentSamples.length;\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Api Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.21/data-model/operations/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You declare queries in the `.wasp` file and implement them using NodeJS.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp not only runs these queries within the server's context but also creates code that enables you to call them from any part of your codebase, whether it's on the client or server side.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To call a Query on the client, you can import it from `wasp/client/operations` and call it directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The usage doesn't change depending on whether the Query is authenticated or not.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp authenticates the logged-in user in the background.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<Tabs groupId="js-ts"> <TabItem value="js" label="JavaScript"> ```js import { getAllTasks, getFilteredTasks } from \'wasp/client/operations\'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Calling a Query on the server is similar to calling it on the client.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's what you have to do differently:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Import Queries from `wasp/server/operations` instead of `wasp/client/operations`.\n'[39m +

                      [32m"- Note that you don't have to pass other parts of the `context` object, like Entities, those will get injected automatically."[39m

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Different ways to get the sessionId for a custom API call - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-21, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1352609018761449552)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Using the Axios wrapper from wasp/client/api The recommended way to make authenticated API calls in Wasp is to use the built-in Axios wrapper that automatically handles authentication for you:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "wasp/client/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async function fetchCustomRoute() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const res = await api.get("/foo/bar");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(res.data);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { api } from "wasp/client/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async function fetchCustomRoute() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const res = await api.get("/foo/bar");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'console.log(res.data);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This wrapper will automatically include the necessary authentication headers, so you don't need to manually extract the session ID from localStorage.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is the cleanest and most secure approach.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Regarding the endpoint to fetch the session ID from the backend, Wasp has an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'/auth/me\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"endpoint that returns session information, but it's not recommended to use this directly for authentication purposes in your API calls.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, use the provided\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'api\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wrapper from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp/client/api\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'----------------------'[39m

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the readFile tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
